transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, what brings me in is that I just keep dodging anything that even smells like my old job. You know, office buildings, security talks, networking events near the work sites... I just stay away from all of it. And if people start asking about the day it happened, I just make some excuse and get out of there. It's just getting to be too much to work around.
How long ago did the day it happened occur?
It was about a year and seven months ago. This has all been going on since I was fired right after that armed incident.
Since the armed incident, have you had unwanted, distressing memories or nightmares about what happened?

Yeah, I do. It happens completely out of nowhere. I'll just be... washing the dishes, or driving past a warehouse gate, and the whole scene just pops back into my head. It's so sharp. I can actually hear the panic in people's voices again, and my chest tightens up just like I'm right back there.
Since the armed incident, have you found yourself feeling persistently negative about yourself, other people, or the world?

Yeah, I have. Mostly about other people. Since it happened, I just catch myself thinking that nobody is really safe to trust anymore. I mean... when even someone you managed, someone you actually tried to help, can just turn around and become dangerous like that... it really changes how you look at everyone else.
Since the armed incident, have you felt unusually watchful or on guard, as if danger could happen at any moment?

Yes, I do. It's... well, whenever I walk into a meeting room, or even just a restaurant, the very first thing I do is look for the exits. I just catch myself watching people's hands, seeing what they're doing. And I always have to pick a seat where nobody can come up behind me. I just can't relax unless I know exactly what's going on around me.
Since the armed incident, have you had difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep?

Yes, I have. Most nights, I just lie there... I'm exhausted, but my mind is completely wired. And when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I end up waking up from these dreams where I hear radios crackling and people shouting. After that, I'm just up. Usually way before daylight. I wake up feeling like I haven't rested at all.
